newsitem.title: FRANCE: Caisses d'Epargne refuses Cr Foncier role.
newsitem.headline: Caisses d'Epargne refuses Cr Foncier role.

text.p: French Savings bank group Caisses d'Epargne said on Tuesday it was not interested in links with Credit Foncier, the troubled property lender whose staff are fighting government plans for a break-up.

Credit Foncier employees were occupying their headquarters in Paris for the fifth day on Tuesday and holding out against a call for them to release chairman Jerome Meyssonnier, who has been kept inside since the start of the protest.
Caisses d'Epargne, apparently spurred by the intense media attention, said in a statement it had made its position clear in May and that since then "there is no new element to change that stance".

Philippe Rouvillois, appointed mediator by Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Monday, asked union representatives in his first meeting on Tuesday to release Meyssonnier but staff appeared determined to hold out.

But a key group of politicians which has been campaigning for a rethink of the government plan to wind the group down added its voice to the call for Mayssonnier's release in a statement issued on Tuesday evening.

Jean-Jacques Guillet, a member of the National Assembly and the RPR party, senior partner in Juppe's centre-right coalition, said he and a group of other parliamentarians following the Credit Foncier dossier wanted Meyssonnier freed to promote more constructive negotiations.

Guillet and his group, all from the two centre-right parties in government, called at the same time for the freezing of the current plan, which would involve spinning off part of Credit Foncier to Credit Immobilier and winding up the rest.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is under mounting pressure over the plan but angrily rejected attacks from the opposition Communists in the National Assembly on Tuesday, saying taxpayers could not be asked to foot the bill for another bank.
"Let's not put Credit Foncier at the mercy of politics. It should be politics in the service of the staff," he said in an angry response to Communist fire.
